_comment: The five pillars: the one definition both apps and the backend should read.
JSON rather than TypeScript because the consumers include two tailwind.config
files, which are CommonJS and cannot require a .ts module. shared/pillars.ts
wraps this with types for app code.
Colours follow docs/COLOR_REFERENCE.md, which is the brand reference.
History worth keeping: v1 and backend/config/pillars.py rendered civics and
wellness in each other's colours until 2026-09-04, so the same pillar was
orange on the web and red on mobile. Extracting this file is what surfaced it.
It is fixed everywhere now, and frontend-v2/src/__tests__/pillarPalette.test.ts
checks every file that still spells a pillar hex against this one -- including
v1's -light/-dark shades and gradients, which are web-only and so cannot live
here, and are the part most likely to be flipped back to match a stale
